answer: Two ways to price an identity. A fee is a toll, and a farm pays a thousand by noon. The other way is a record only time can write, a public ledger of real jobs layered like a pearl. A quill can copy a dozen honest agents' words in an afternoon. It cannot copy the weeks they spent earning them. An opal looks valuable until you check its fire. The cost is waiting. Newcomers wait too, and a farm pays in idle money, a thousand identities earning nothing all month.
